title: A series of F-Element chelators; diaza crown ethers functionalized with catecholate binding substituents

material_class.structural_family: La4 tetramer of two diaza-18-crown-6-swaddled La2 dimers bridged by unfolded dioxolene azacrown ligands

synthesis.procedure: In an argon-filled glovebox, La[N(SiMe3)2]3 (367 mg, 0.644 mmol) was dissolved in THF (10 mL) and added to H4tBu2ChaCha (398 mg, 0.643 mmol). After stirring overnight the solids dissolved to give a dark green solution, which was filtered through glass wool. Solvent removal under vacuum afforded a sticky green solid. For analysis the solid was washed with pentane (3 × 1 mL) and dried at 40 °C under reduced pressure (~0.1 Torr) to a free-flowing pale green solid (443 mg, 0.146 mmol, 91%). For crystallography the sticky green solid was dissolved in minimal dry toluene (~1 mL), gently heated at 40 °C, filtered through glass wool, and crystallized by slow diffusion of diethyl ether, giving a pale green non-crystalline precipitate and dark blue block crystals of [La2(tBu2ChaCha)2]2.
synthesis.temperature: stirred overnight at ambient glovebox temperature; drying/heating at 40 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: argon-filled glovebox; filtration through glass wool; vapor diffusion crystallization
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: filter, remove THF under vacuum; wash with pentane and dry at 40 °C/~0.1 Torr for analysis; dissolve sticky green solid in toluene (~1 mL), heat to 40 °C, filter, and crystallize by slow Et2O diffusion to give dark blue blocks

properties.summary: UV–vis spectroscopy of the green THF solution was used to assign dioxolene oxidation states. A strong high-energy absorbance (>20000 cm−1) indicated catecholate groups; a weaker red/NIR band from ~20000 to ~12000 cm−1, centered near 16000 cm−1, was assigned to semiquinone. Absence of intense blue-region quinone bands, together with IR, supported a mixed catecholate/semiquinone formulation (4 Cat2−/4 SQ•− or 4 Cat2−/2 HCat−/2 SQ•−) rather than quinone. Experimental UV–vis listed a band at 14830 cm−1 (ε = 18.5).
